question: Name the employee of the East India Company who deciphered Asokan Brahmi in 1830s.
solution:
The correct answer is __**James Prinsep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• James Prinsep, an employee of the East India Company, successfully deciphered the Brahmi script in the 1830s.
 
• He identified the inscriptions on the pillars and rock edicts of Ashoka, facilitating the understanding of ancient Indian history.
 
• The decipherment of Brahmi script was a monumental breakthrough in epigraphy and the study of ancient Indian scripts.
 
• James Prinsep published his findings in the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, which significantly advanced the field of Indian epigraphy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmi Script:**

 
 
• One of the oldest writing systems used in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is the ancestor of most of the modern scripts of South and Southeast Asia.
 
• It was used primarily during the Maurya and Gupta periods.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka:**
 
 
• The third emperor of the Maurya Dynasty who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He is remembered for his propagation of Buddhism and his inscriptions on pillars and rocks.
 
• Ashoka's edicts provide valuable insights into his reign and policies.
 
 
 
• **Epigraphy:**
 
 
• The study of inscriptions or epigraphs as writing.
 
• It is a primary tool for understanding ancient civilizations and their languages.
 
• Epigraphists analyze historical inscriptions to reconstruct historical events and understand cultural contexts.
 
 
 
• **Asiatic Society of Bengal:**
 
 
• Founded in 1784 by Sir William Jones in Kolkata.
 
• It played a crucial role in the development of the study of Asian history, culture, and literature.
 
• The society's journal was a prominent publication for scholarly research during the 19th century.
